utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, they were not buried in mass gravesites.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, one technical question just in order to clarify one date. It's quite a specific question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. You can ask that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said that you buried those dead on the 31st of March and 1st of April. Do you know that Amnesty International at Kukes in Albania was told by a person, Citaku, who said that on the 8th of April -- there are three different dates; the 8th of April, the 4th of April, and the 3rd of April. So all of these persons, these three different persons, said that they took part in the burial ceremony, and they gave Amnesty International investigators these three dates, 8th of April, 4th of April, the 3rd of April. But you are giving a different date, the 31st of March and the 1st of April. And did you hear about the names of these people?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter was not able to get the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do you know anything about what's being alleged? If you don't, just say so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know nothing more than what I just said. I know that this massacre was -- this massacre happened in March 1999, and the burial took place on the 1st of April of the same year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tapuskovic, before you begin your cross-examination, it should be noted, in case it's considered elsewhere, that the accused had over 80 minutes cross-examination on this occasion. Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I will do my best to be as brief as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, Mr. Loshi, whether we clarified one point, actually a point we heard a moment ago and which you stated previously that all the victims of the conflict which were brought in from other places, could you tell us how many of them were there? Did you ever learn how many persons were brought in from other areas, from other places, to the particular spot where you filmed them?

utterances.speaker: LIRI LOSHI
utterances.text: The word "conflict" doesn't mean clash. "Conflict" means conflict between Serbian forces with the civilian Albanian population from the start of the war until the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not insisting upon the fighting. Can you just explain to me whether you ever learnt how many people from other places where people had lost their lives, if they weren't killed on that spot, how many of those people who were brought in from other areas to the particular spot where they were buried.

utterances.speaker: LIRI LOSHI
utterances.text: The people who were brought were also from the village of Izbica but rather more distant from the place where the massacre took place. But -- at a distance. But nobody else was killed elsewhere, that is, in another village, was brought to Izbica. All the victims were from Izbica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that, but they weren't killed in that particular spot. They were brought in from elsewhere, somewhere else where they had in fact been killed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LIRI LOSHI
utterances.text: They were brought from several places where they were found around the massacred group, only a few metres away. So the number of those massacred was about 100. And I didn't count them personally. I can't state about this. And these others were brought from other places but still within the village of Izbica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You explained it differently here, but I don't wish to insist upon the matter. I leave it to the Court to decide. But here's another example, Mr. Loshi: On page 24 of your statement dated September the 24th where you give an overview, there's a name that crops up. Ali Beqiri is the name, and in your comments you state that he was a KLA fighter, KLA soldier killed after the massacre. So you say in this particular place that it was a KLA soldier who was killed after the massacre who was in fact buried at that- burial site, at that spot. And it is on page 24 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: LIRI LOSHI
utterances.text: It's true that Ajet Beqiri, and not only him but Asim Bajrami, both soldiers of the KLA who were in Izbica on that day were killed on the 27th of March that day, that is, one day before the massacre. And they were buried in one place with the victims of the massacre. I said that before, and I've said it again. So they weren't killed on the 28th.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But you say here that he was killed after the massacre, not before, and you've recorded it here in the column. You say that he was killed after the massacre, not before; right?

utterances.speaker: LIRI LOSHI
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that anywhere. Please bring me the statement so that I can read it. I said that they were buried after the massacre.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: It says here in your comments, in column titled "Comments" in B/C/S, it says: "KLA soldier killed after the massacre." It is on page 24 of the English version, and I think it coincides with your own version, and it says"Killed after the massacre."

utterances.speaker: LIRI LOSHI
utterances.text: I absolutely deny this. It's not true that they were killed after the massacre and nor did I state this. They were killed one day before the massacre, on the 27th of March, and they weren't killed in the place where the civilian population was gathered but much further away.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So what it states in your statement is not right, is not correct; is that it?

utterances.speaker: LIRI LOSHI
utterances.text: If it is - and once again, I doubt that is written in my statement, but if it is, it's not true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Show the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this part about the statement is not a bit which I've read because it's not related to my statement. And this is a mistake that has entered and has nothing -- has nothing to do with my statement. It's no doubt a mistake by the person who was talking to me, because it's not in my actual statement which I gave. This is not said anywhere in my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Yes. Let the statement go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, along with these documents that were handed over to you today as well, you have the last page in that set of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Loshi, there's a statement there which you gave on the 15th of June 2002 to the International Tribunal for serious violations of international criminal law, and in that statement and on that page, you state that: "In addition to what I have stated in the previous statements, I should like to add that in 1998, I assisted the KLA," because you helped the wounded soldiers. That's quite understandable. "And I joined that organisation in August 1998 as well. I bore a rifle for my own protection but I never fired at anyone." Is that true and correct as it is stated in your statement?

utterances.speaker: LIRI LOSHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And one more point I would like to clarify, and that is the following: In your statement dated September, and it is on page 3 of the English version, last paragraph, and then page 4, second paragraph, and page 4, paragraph 4, in which you said the following: First of all, you said that you knew that the Serb forces were in the area but that on the 21st, 22nd and 23rd of March there were no major episodes. So you didn't see any members of the army during those three days, and there were no incidents during those three days, as you state here; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LIRI LOSHI
utterances.text: It's true that in the place where I was living, that is in the villages round about, I saw no Serbian soldiers in those days, and I saw no fighting between the KLA and the Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And then you go on to say that on the 25th of March, people started to concentrate, to group in the Izbica valley, and by the 26th of March, "I estimated that there were about 25.000 people gathered there." You make no mention of seeing either soldiers or members of the police force there when these people gathered there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LIRI LOSHI
utterances.text: It is true that on the 25th of March, 1999, Serbian shells arriving from the direction of Runik and Banja killed three civilians in the village of Klladernice where the population had initially been concentrated, and from that day on there was a movement of the population towards Izbica which was considered a slightly safer area. But it's true that I didn't see Serbian soldiers on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: No. That was on the 24th of March. What you're talking about took place on the 24th of March, and that's what you said, and that the people had taken refuge in the schoolhouse. But on the 25th of March, 25.000 people were gathered there. Now, nearby were there any police or military forces there? Because you make no mention of them here.

utterances.speaker: LIRI LOSHI
utterances.text: It's true that this happened on the 24th. This is my error. Because it happened on the end of the day. And I went in the morning of the 25th of March to see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but on the 25th of March, when there was this group of people numbering 25.000, at that place at that time, there were no soldiers or policemen there, were there? Right?

utterances.speaker: LIRI LOSHI
utterances.text: No. No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And is that what the situation was like on the 29th of March as well when there were 30.000 people and KLA members? There were no soldiers or policemen there either. There were 30.000 people on the 29th of March. Were there any soldiers or policemen there? Now, if the KLA was there, probably the army wasn't.

utterances.speaker: LIRI LOSHI
utterances.text: Let me explain things. On the 29th of March, I'm talking about Tushile, not Izbica because in Izbica the massacre happened on the previous day, on the 28th, but if you're thinking of the village of Tushile, then it's true that on this day to which you refer there were no Serbian policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Very briefly, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Dr. Loshi, during the course of cross-examination, it has been suggested to you, inter alia, that the three groups that you filmed and that were shown on the edited tape prepared from the master tape, that these bodies were of KLA soldiers who had been gathered from other areas who had been killed during military conflicts and brought to Izbica. At least, that's my understanding of the cross-examination. That being the suggestion, I have two questions that follow. You have already told us that these individuals appear to be -- I believe the words you used were "of an advanced age." Is that your observation of the bodies that you filmed when you produced this film?

utterances.speaker: LIRI LOSHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: There appear to be men on crutches as well, elderly men on crutches. Was there those type of individuals in at least two of the groups that are filmed?

utterances.speaker: LIRI LOSHI
utterances.text: Yes, there were, but mainly in the first group, that is the western group, there were certain handicapped people. But there were also handicapped people in the other group, and there were several, not just two or three, but quite a number. There were people with various handicaps, both physical and mental.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: In your experience, were the normal KLA soldiers men of advanced age and handicapped people on crutches?

utterances.speaker: LIRI LOSHI
utterances.text: No. The majority, the overwhelming majority of the members of the KLA were very young. And people of this age, which we see in the scenes that I brought to this court, they were not KLA people at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Did you notice any uniform or insignia indicating membership in the KLA on any of the bodies that you videotaped?

utterances.speaker: LIRI LOSHI
utterances.text: In the groups, the three groups of the massacred people in which you can see, I did not see any insignia of this kind. During the burial, I noticed one soldier lying by the grave, in a KLA uniform, and this man was Ajet Beqiri who had been my friend and was also from my home village, but I did not see any other uniformed person. As I said, he was killed one day earlier, on the 27th.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: As a medical doctor, are you able to determine -- were you able to make an observation as to whether or not these bodies that you looked at had been killed, shall we say, as early as the first week in March, or was the state of their decomposition, so to speak, such that they were recently killed, within the last two or three days?

utterances.speaker: LIRI LOSHI
utterances.text: On the basis of a superficial examination, which is all that was possible during war conditions, it was easy to see that these bodies had not been killed a long time before but had been quite recently killed, that is, two days, as I had been told by the women whom I'd spoken to slightly earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Do I also understand you correctly to have told the Court on cross-examination that you had spoken to some of these individuals whom you recognised within the two or three days preceding to filming their dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: LIRI LOSHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: My final question, sir: You've told us, both in the statement and under cross-examination, about the actual videotapes, and you talked about differences in format and then re-recording. The first format of the original tape, I'm holding up a very small videotape. Would you look at it, please. Is that the original format of the tape which was designated as 1733, is that the format of the original tape?

utterances.speaker: LIRI LOSHI
utterances.text: From the format that I can see from here, I can't make it out all that clearly, but it could well be the cassette that I brought to this court.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Then I'm holding up a larger, normal size videotape that is usually in use at video stores, et cetera. Is that the size of videotape that you recorded or re-recorded what was on the smaller tape? Is that the two different sizes?

utterances.speaker: LIRI LOSHI
utterances.text: Which one, the small one or the big one?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Now looking at a bigger one.

utterances.speaker: LIRI LOSHI
utterances.text: Yes. That's the size of the cassette that I used to transfer the material from the small cassette to the large one, because later I used a small cassette of the kind that you're holding in your other hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, in light of the extensive cross-examination and in light of other evidence such as from Dr. Baccard about observations he made from the original videotape, 1733, you have only at the moment received the small edited four-minute tape. I would like to tender, without playing, the original and a copy of tape 1733.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It would be part of the exhibit which contains the extracts.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you. Those are all my questions under the circumstances. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the extract will be Prosecutor's Exhibit 308A, and the originals will be given Prosecutor's Exhibit 308.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an additional question. May I put it? It is connected to what Mr. Ryneveld just asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. We must have some order in this. You must ask your cross-examination, then the other side have a right to re-examine. When you come to witnesses, the same will be applied to you, but you can't simply ask questions in any order you like. Dr. Liri, thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give your evidence. It's now concluded. You are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution calls as its next witness, Mr. Caslav Golubovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. If you would like to take a seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you please tell the Court your full name, first name followed by your last.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Caslav Golubovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, were you born on the 15th of May, 1937?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And you are a Serb and by religion an Eastern Orthodox Christian; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, were you, in 1999, the chief of the Secretariat for Internal Affairs in Bor in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And while you were in that position, was a refrigerator truck containing corpses found in the Danube in an area within the jurisdiction of the Bor SUP? And by "SUP" I'm using the Serbian acronym for the Secretariat for Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Before we get to this incident, I'm going to ask you a few background questions. You are currently retired. Is that correct, Mr. Mr. Golubovic?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: When did you retire?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of January. The 1st of January, 2001, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And what rank did you hold in the MUP, the Ministry of Internal Affairs, when you retired?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: The rank of colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Just prior to retirement, were you the chief of the SUP in Bor?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: How long did you occupy that position?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: For about ten years. From 1992 onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please describe to the Court where -- where is Bor, the town of Bor, and the area of responsibility of the SUP in Bor.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Bor is situated in Eastern Serbia. It is the SUP area, and it borders with Romania and Bulgaria.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Approximately how many staff in the MUP would have been under your jurisdiction as the chief of the SUP in Bor, approximately, as far as you can recall?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: It depended, but it ranged between 600 and 700 people. Those were the number of people working in the secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And below the level of the secretariat in Bor, were there -- were there smaller police stations in several of the municipalities?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: In all the municipalities there were police stations or local police departments within the frameworks of the overall secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And how many of these -- how many of these police stations below the level of the secretariat would have been within the jurisdiction of the Bor SUP?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there was the Bor municipality with the station in Negotin in Majdanpek and Kladovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Prior to becoming the chief of the SUP in Bor, Mr. Golubovic, you held various positions in the MUP, beginning in 1982 when you joined the MUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I was an employee of the Ministry of the Interior, and I held different posts and was given different assignments. Before that, I was head of the secretariat in Zajecar, and from that post I came to Bor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And prior to 1982, I believe you held several positions, including positions in the municipal administration in Bor and also in the copper mining and smelting plant near Bor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I worked in the Municipal Assembly of Bor and in the ATB factory combine in Bor up until 1982.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And is it correct that you have a university degree in law which you obtained in 1962 and that in 1973 you passed the bar examination?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic where were you on the 6th of April in 1999 at around 6.30 in the evening?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I was in Bor, at my house on Lake Bor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did you receive a telephone call at about that time? Just yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And did you recognise the voice of the caller? Just yes or no to that question as well, please.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: How did you recognise -- how did you recognise that voice?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I recognised the voice because the man came through. He said his name, and we have had daily contacts, so I knew his voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And who was -- who did you recognise that voice -- whose voice did you recognise that to be?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: It was the head of the crime department in the secretariat. His name was Tomislav Miladinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: As the chief of the SUP in Bor, Mr. Golubovic, are you his immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And what would the scope of responsibility be of Mr. Miladinovic as the head of the crime police?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the responsibilities were provided for in the rules of service, but it was up to him to organise the business of the department and to lead the professional part in the sense, first and foremost, of crime detection, general crime, economic crimes, filing, reports, and everything linked to crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And this would be throughout the area of responsibility of the SUP in Bor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Going back to the telephone call now. What subject matter was Mr. Miladinovic calling you about?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: He was calling to convey information to me that, immediately prior to that, he had received information from Kladovo to the effect that a refrigerator truck was pulled out onto the bank, which was flowing down the Danube, floating down the Danube, and when they opened the refrigerator truck, they found a number of dead bodies, between 20 and 30 corpses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And when you say that the information was received from Kladovo, could you specify whether Mr. Miladinovic indicated where exactly from Kladovo he was receiving that information?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: From the SUP department in Kladovo. Probably from the duty officer or the head of the department.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And did Mr. Miladinovic indicate or other -- did he tell you where specifically this refrigerator truck had been located?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: He said that it had been located in the village of Tekija on the Danube.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did he indicate whether any investigation into this incident had been undertaken up to that point, however brief that investigation may have been?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: He said that they had tried to carry out an on-the-spot investigation and that there were municipal officials and public prosecutor and the municipal investigating judge and a team of people from the department and that they had been pulling out the refrigerator truck throughout the day, that in the afternoon when he himself received that information, when they had opened the door and when they saw the 20 or 30 bodies, as they said, which were inside, because of the darkness and impending darkness, the on-the-spot investigation was interrupted and the municipal prosecutor and the investigating judge didn't wish to conduct the investigation because they thought it came under the jurisdiction of the district prosecution office.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: How long did this telephone call last?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Five to ten minutes, most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And during that telephone call, did you -- did you say anything to Mr. Miladinovic?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I told him that I will leave the lake right away, that I will come to pick him up in Bor, and that we will leave for Kladovo so that I could inform myself in detail, to see what it was all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And did you then go to Kladovo after that?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, what time did you arrive in Kladovo?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in view of the distance, most probably at around twenty to -- twenty or twenty hours and thirty, so around 8.30 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And where specifically in Kladovo did you go?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: We went to the chief office of the department.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And by "department" -- perhaps this is a translation issue; by "department," do you mean the police station in Kladovo?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: When you arrived at the police station in Kladovo, were there people already present there? Just yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Could you -- could you tell us who was present, their position and their name.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: The chief of the department was there, Sperlic. Then also the chief of the crime department was there, Milan -- I cannot remember everybody's name right now. Then there was the municipal public prosecutor, the municipal investigative judge. Slobodan Aleksic was there. He was the head of the state security centre. There was another employee of the state security centre. So this is more or less the group of people that was there. Perhaps someone else might have been there also.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Golubovic, whether there was anyone present from the border police station?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The station commander was there also, Mitrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Golubovic, after you arrived at the Kladovo police station, did you then have a meeting with these persons?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: When I arrived, I first asked to be informed about what it was all about, what had happened the day before and that day, what they had done in view of the fact that this is in the territory of Kladovo. What did the department do, what activities did it undertake, in order to receive all of this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If we could go through the substance of that process of informing you. Were you informed how the refrigerator truck was discovered?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And what were you informed about how it was discovered?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: They told me that the day before, a citizen noticed that an object was floating down the Danube and that this was reported to the officials in the Kladovo department. They were unable to identify this object on that day and that is why they reported it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And during this meeting in the Kladovo police station, who was it that informed you of this among the participants in that meeting?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I was informed by the chief of the department and most probably by somebody else who was present, who was updated about some other matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: By the chief of the department, you're speaking of Mr. Sperlic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did Mr. Sperlic inform you also on the day upon which this refrigerator truck was discovered?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He informed me. That was how it began, by this being reported by a citizen, that this was reported, and then the team went out to the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Maybe my question didn't come through clearly. Which day were you told the truck had been discovered?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: On the 6th of April in the evening. That's when I was informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. And you're speaking, of course, about this meeting in the Kladovo police station. Just to be -- just --

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Just to be clear, which -- were you told upon which day the truck itself had been found by the -- first of all, noticed by the citizen -- by the citizen and then discovered by the Kladovo police?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: It was noticed on the 5th of April for the first time, and that was the first time that it was reported to the department of internal affairs. I came to Kladovo on the 6th, in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying that. And referring only to the events on the 5th of April as they were reported to you during this meeting, what did the OUP, which is the Serbian acronym for police station in Kladovo, what did they do in response? Did they undertake any actions?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, they just said that this object which was floating down the Danube, that they reached this object, that it was tethered to a tree on the bank. All of this was happening in the afternoon, so there was no possibility to undertake any other actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And what further action, if any, were you informed that the Kladovo police took with regards to this refrigerator truck on the 6th of April? In other words, earlier on in the day upon which you were having this meeting.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Measures were undertaken on the 6th of April to drag this object out on the bank. A machine was used for this, a crane from the hydroelectric power station Djerdap. So the time was spent in attempts to pull this object out of the Danube. When it was partially dragged out to the bank, the investigative team came from Kladovo with the public prosecutor and the investigating judge. This occurred in view of the problems that they had encountered and the conditions; there was war, planes were flying over all the time. So this happened sometime in the late afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And during the course of the 6th of April, were you informed whether the team of people at the site of the refrigerator truck had looked inside the refrigerator truck?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I was informed that when they wanted to start the investigation, when they opened the door, I said in the beginning that they observed a number of corpses. At that point, the number they were talking about was from between 20 to 30. They immediately closed the door and nothing else was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, at this meeting in the Kladovo police station, were the people present there, did they make any assumptions that they informed you of as to who these bodies were, these corpses?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Everyone had their own opinion, starting from the fact that there was an inscription on the truck, "Prizren," and allegedly when they opened that, they could see clothing. There were assumptions that these were most probably dead bodies from Kosovo, but nobody explicitly said that. They were just assumptions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Just to clarify that, when you say that no one explicitly said that, did they at least indicate what their assumptions were?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Since the bodies at that point were seen by only two or three people, these others didn't know anything else. So except for their comments, there was nothing else. As far as I was informed, this was only seen by the public prosecutor and the investigative judge for a moment and the crime technician from Kladovo, the person who was doing this job. The rest of those present, I think, were actually not at the location, and they were only able to give their comments. At that point, they were not eyewitnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: As far as you can recall, what was it that was said about the clothing that would have led to the assumption you indicated?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: It was said that these were female bodies, that they were wearing dimije, pantaloons, and that many bodies were wearing suits which indicated that they came from down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And just to clarify, when you say "down there," you mean Kosovo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to move on, Mr. Shin, now to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did you at some point report this matter? I'm sorry, I didn't understand you correctly, Your Honour. I am actually about to move on to another topic, so this would be a convenient time for a break, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, we'll break now. Mr. Golubovic, we're going to adjourn now for 20 minutes for a short break. Would you remember, please, in this adjournment and any others there may be in this case in your evidence not to speak to anybody about your evidence until it's over, and that does include the members of the prosecution team. Could you be back, please, in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, just prior to the break, you were testifying about matters discussed during the meeting in the Kladovo police station at about 8.30. Did you at some point report this matter, including the results of these discussions, with your superiors? Just yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And by what means did you make this report?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: By telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Before we go to the contents of this report, I'm going to ask you a few preliminary questions. Focusing on the telephone number, what -- what number did you call, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. And was it a telephone number provided to you by the Ministry of Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: It was the telephone number of the head of the state security at the ministry. I don't remember the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Actually, just to check on the translation there, was that the state security?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: It was the chief of the public security, General Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: What time did you make this call?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I made the call shortly after I had been apprised of the situation. After I was informed about the situation, I conveyed the information to him and asked him what we should do and how we should do it. I asked for instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, let's just take this step-by-step. Do you remember, as far as you can remember, approximately what time was that call made?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Most probably between 8.30 to 9.00, after I had been informed. And the amount of time it took for me to be informed was about 15 to 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And when you made the call, did you recognise the voice on the other end of the telephone line?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: How did you recognise that voice?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I recognised it because I had heard it many times before in other contacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And who did you recognise that voice as belonging to?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Like I said, it was the voice of the chief of the public security service, General Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Was General Djordjevic your immediate supervisor?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, going to the substance of this telephone call, what did you -- what did you say to General Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I conveyed to him what was said to me in Kladovo at this meeting; that the day before, this refrigerator truck was found, and that on that first day, until the refrigerator truck was opened, basically everybody thought that this about a traffic accident that had happened on the road that goes along the Danube. I conveyed to him that on that day it was partially pulled out with a crane, that it was opened, and that 20 to 30 corpses were found inside, that the justice organs were there, the prosecutor and the investigative judge, that no -- no investigation was carried out. They did not feel that they were authorised to do that. They informed their superiors about it, the district investigating organs. So this is what I conveyed to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, did you also convey to him the assumption of some people in that earlier meeting that the corpses were persons from Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And did you convey to General Djordjevic also the -- what was written on the truck as well as a description of the clothing of some of the bodies, as you were informed during the previous meeting?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I told him that, that the truck bore this inscription and that I was told that the corpses were dressed in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: What was General Djordjevic's initial reaction upon being told about these things by you?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I had the impression that he was surprised. So ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: How did you -- on what basis did you inform that impression that he was surprised?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Based on the conversation itself, his reactions during the conversations. He used certain terms that we use.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Could you just explain? You don't necessarily have to repeat those words, but could you explain what terms you mean, what kinds of terms?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: A number of those terms are perhaps not appropriate for this occasion, but, "Oh, it's not possible." "Not really." Something to that effect, indicating that this information, this event, comes as a surprise to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: As General Djordjevic is your superior, did you seek his instructions or orders with regards to this matter?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I said a little earlier that I was asking for instructions. I was asking to be told what I should do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And what did he say in reply?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: He said that we would talk in about 15 or 20 minutes and then that he would tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did a telephone call in fact come later?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And it was made -- it was made to -- to the police station in Kladovo where you were?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: A few preliminary questions again before we get to the contents of that telephone call. First, who answered the telephone?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. Perhaps I did, perhaps the chief of the police station did since we were sitting at his desk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And did you recognise the voice on the other end of the telephone?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Whose voice was it?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: It was the voice of General Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: What did General Djordjevic tell you then?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: General Djordjevic told me to try, in the course of the night, to transfer the corpses from the refrigerator truck to a different vehicle and to explore the possibility of burying the corpses somewhere in the area of Kladovo. He said that that was the order of the minister. And the general instructions were to this effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: When General Djordjevic told you that was the order of the minister, just to clarify, could you tell us which minister you're speaking of.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: About the Minister of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: It was the late Vlajko Stojiljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did General Djordjevic give you any other instructions regarding the refrigerator truck?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly now whether it was during this second conversation or during subsequent conversation in the course of that night. Instructions were given to the effect that this object, this refrigerator truck, should be destroyed later, that information is not released, that none of us are to give any statements to the press or to the TV. These were additional orders, instructions, or tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And just to clarify, Mr. Golubovic, with regards to the destruction of the refrigerator truck and the restriction against release of information, did General Djordjevic indicate whether those were also instructions from the minister?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: When he told me all of that, he said that all of this was said by the minister. He referred back to this being stated by the minister. The minister probably told him that or he said that the minister told him that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, did you then convey these instructions from General Djordjevic to the persons at the Kladovo police station?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Was action in fact then taken to carry out these instructions?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Then we agreed how to bring the refrigerator truck up from the edge of the river, how to get it up onto the road; it was 30 to 40 metres away from the river. It was very difficult to pull it out. They were not able to do that the day before. And that the next day we needed to have a larger piece of machinery which could achieve that. We were actually talking about all of this during subsequent conversations, but that at that time, we were talking about how to get the corpses out of the refrigerator truck. There were several matters: How to get the bodies out of the refrigerator truck, the vehicle that we were supposed to provide, where to bury them. We were talking about all of these different technical matters; to provide blankets and sheets for the transport of these bodies, to explore the possibilities since the instructions were such, to bury them somewhere in Kladovo where we were able to. So we undertook certain actions in relation to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, what -- in particular, what was done to get manpower to carry out these tasks?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: The utility company was asked to provide a certain number of employees who would be able to carry that out, because the day before, these employees were taken from the utility company when it was still thought that this was a traffic accident. So they were kept prepared in case they were needed for certain activities relating to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Could you please tell us the name of the utility company and what kind of company it was.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I think the name was Komunalac Kladovo, which is a utilities company dealing with all the communal services required by the town, and it is under their competence, I suppose, that the burial takes place, burials in Kladovo in care of the cemetery and so on and offering that kind of service.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, after these actions had been -- were under way, did you stay in Kladovo or did you then move elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: We stayed in Kladovo for a while, until the vehicle was taken to Tekija and all the technical matters seen to. And then later on, we started out for Tekija ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And when you refer to this vehicle taken to Tekija, are you referring to this -- what are you referring to actually?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the vehicle was taken from Kladovo and the communal service, the utility service, to Tekija, and we were going to transport the bodies in that vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And just to clarify, that vehicle, was that a truck?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you then report these developments again at some point?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we arrived in Tekija at about half past eleven at night. We went into the police station and their offices there, the premises they have in Tekija, and I was told once again what had happened from the time in Kladovo when we started thinking about how to deal with the situation, what had been actually done, and then towards midnight, half past eleven or perhaps later, I can't give you an exact time, I once again called up General Djordjevic and conveyed all this updated information to him and some of our requirements.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Specifically now just focusing on what you told General Djordjevic. First of all, approximately what time was this telephone call made?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: The telephone conversation took place at around 11.30 at night, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. And focusing, then, on what you told General Djordjevic, what did you tell General Djordjevic with regards to the burial of the bodies?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I told him that people were working to extract the bodies from the refrigerator truck on the banks and that they were loading them up onto the lorry, the truck, that it was a difficult task, and it was difficult to do it because it was dark, that there were no lights to be used, in view of the general situation that prevailed, and that transferring these bodies was difficult because it was a steep embankment, that it was heavy-duty work, difficult to do - that's what I was told - and that up until that point in time, just one of the bodies had been transported and transferred and we were still -- it was still considered that there were 20 to 30 of these corpses. However, when the first bodies were taken out, it was seen that there were more than 30 bodies in the refrigerator truck, and it became clear that the job wouldn't be -- wouldn't be finished by morning. That's what I conveyed to the general. And I also told him that I considered that we didn't have either the technical ability or the experts we needed to identify the bodies or to perform the autopsies on those bodies. And during that conversation - and he agreed to what I said - I also said that the best thing would be to send the bodies to Belgrade or Nis where there is a forensics institute.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If I could ask you a specific question about that. When you made that suggestion, what was General Djordjevic's initial reaction?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I put forward this proposal of mine, but the request was that his initial order stand, that what he said to begin with should be carried out, and that meant burying the bodies somewhere in Kladovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did you then pursue your suggestion further with him?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I insisted that this should not take place in Kladovo but that it should take place elsewhere where the conditions were better, where there were all the facilities to conduct these things, and where it would be easier to ensure the conditions necessary, because here there were -- there were the remnants of the bombardments and all the rest of it. It was difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: When you insisted, did General Djordjevic say anything further in response to your suggestion?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: No. On that occasion, he should that we should finish the job and that we should speak to each other once that had been done.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Approximately how long was that telephone call, this telephone call from Tekija?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly, but I assume, once again, that this was ten minutes. We tried to make our conversations as brief as possible, without going into any superfluous explanations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Going back to the work that was being done at the site of the refrigerator truck now, following this conversation, did the workers complete loading the bodies during that night?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the workers worked up until 0200 hours, I believe, and then they had a pause. This was interrupted. And up until that time, some 30 corpses had been loaded up onto the lorry, onto the truck. I think the people were far too tired by that time to be able to do any more work.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did you at some point after that, update your superior again as to the developments with the refrigerator truck?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When we realised that it was impossible to carry on the work - and this was at 0200 hours - I phoned up the general again and reported back to him as to what had been done, and I told him that we had finished the job for that day or for that night, that that's as far as we had been able to get. And then in that conversation, I insisted again, I prevailed upon him again that the bodies should be taken to places where there were better facilities to carry out everything that had to be carried out; determination of identity, autopsies, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, just on that specific point again, what did General Djordjevic tell you at this point in response to your suggestion, your repetition of your suggestion, rather?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: He accepted that. It was the last conversation we had that particular night. He agreed, and he said that the truck with the bodies should start out for Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And during this conversation, was there any discussion of another truck being used?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As we did not have any trucks free down in that area, I asked him to secure another truck from the ministry which would be able to carry the remaining bodies the next day and so that the bodies could be transported in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And with regards to sending the truck that you already had at the scene towards Belgrade, were any discussions made about the arrangements by which that should be done?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was said that they should set off for Belgrade. And whether he was called or somebody else was called to whom I could give the mobile telephone number of the driver and the number plates so that an escort could be organised or so that somebody else could escort the truck to Belgrade, all I knew was that Belgrade was the destination that was given.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, when did you leave Tekija that morning?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: The truck left at about 2030 hours -- 0230 hours, that is to say 2.30 a.m., and we discussed what should be done to finish the job, to load up the rest of the bodies and also where the bodies should be taken to once they reached Belgrade and what the people from Kladovo, from the police station there, what was in store for them that day, what they had to do, what work to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And after having done that, what time did you yourself leave Tekija?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Towards morning. Whether it was 4.00 or 5.00 a.m., I can't remember exactly, but I left for Kladovo and stopped off at the police station. At 7.00 a.m., I was on the job in Bor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So you did not get any sleep that night; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did you learn afterwards whether the remaining bodies in the refrigerator truck were also pulled out of the refrigerator truck?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: The following evening or the next day in the morning, I was informed from Kladovo that on that day, that is to say it was the 7th in the evening, that the rest of the bodies had been loaded up into the truck that had been sent from the ministry and that the truck was on its way to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And who was it that informed you of this?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I was informed by the head of the department in Kladovo, Miladinovic. He was the contact person on the phone mostly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, you had also testified earlier that General Djordjevic instructed you that the refrigerator truck was to be destroyed. Were you informed afterwards whether or not it was in fact destroyed?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I think that the refrigerator truck was transferred to the Komunalac company, where it remained for several days, and that it was destroyed subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Who was it that informed you of that? Specifically that it was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Once again, the department head in Kladovo, because he was the only one that was -- had the authority and down the chain to inform me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And were you informed also how the refrigerator truck was destroyed?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: They said that they tried to set fire to it first, and as that didn't succeed in destroying it, I think some explosives were used to destroy it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you recall where it was that it was destroyed, the location?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: The refrigerator truck was driven off to the Petrovo Selo training ground, somewhere there, and that's where it was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, with regards to the payment for the workers during that night, did you do anything in that regard following the work of that evening?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not getting the interpretation, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. I'll put the question to you again. Following the work that was done that night, did you do anything with regards to payment for the workers who were carrying out the work that night? Do we have a translation now?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Try again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm getting it now, thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Golubovic, the question was: Following the work that was done that night, did you do anything with regards to payment for the workers who had carried out those actions?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Well, after some time went by, I asked the ministry to give me some money to be able to pay the workers for the work they'd done, and we received that money, that is to say 10.000 dinars, and we distributed it to the workers who had done the work.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Approximately how many workers was that?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know; four, perhaps six.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Who specifically did you ask for these funds, these 10.000 dinars?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: The general.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Just to be clear, what was the name of the general?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: General Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall who actually gave you -- gave you these funds?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I think his name was Aleksic. He was an employee of the ministry. And the funds were given to me. I gave it straight on to Toma Miladinovic, who went to Kladovo and paid out the workers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And were these funds provided in cash?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Regarding the -- regarding these events on the evening and early morning of April 6th and 7th, did you at any point issue any report in writing, setting out what had happened?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Is there any reason why you did not set out a report in writing?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: The reason was that all communication had been destroyed. And I think that the ministry building had been destroyed a few days prior to that, so there were no -- there was no communication, and all that was left to us by way of communication was the telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, were you at some point interviewed by members of a working group headed by Dragan Karleusa regarding this matter? Just yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you recall when that was, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was in the middle of 1991. Approximately. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And prior to being interviewed by that working group, did you hear of any other police or judicial investigations into the refrigerator truck incident -- into this refrigerator truck incident?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. No. Not as far as I know. I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And given your competence as the chief of the SUP in Bor, an investigation of that -- of that kind, is that something that you would have been informed about?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Well, while I was working, probably it would have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: While you were the chief of the SUP in Bor, were you aware at some point of an article about this refrigerator truck published in a newspaper called the "Timok Crime Review"?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I think that the Krimi newspaper, although it's not one I read, did write about it. There was an article, I was told, where something had been written, but whether that was a conversation with General Djordjevic saying that he had been informed and then him having told me or whether I heard something about this and conveyed it to him, that was the gist of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So did you at some point discuss this article with General Djordjevic, then?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And whether it was you who informed him or he informed you, do you recall what his reaction was to the publication of this article?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Well, both his reaction and my reaction was that it was unnecessary and not a good thing for the papers to write about things like that, but -- and that this should be something that the state organs should do and see to and not the general press at large.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Are you aware that -- whether the state organs at any point while you were the chief of the SUP in Bor did actually publish anything regarding the refrigerator truck incident?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't really remember -- or I don't know. I didn't read anything to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Golubovic, you had mentioned in one of your telephone conversations with General Djordjevic during the night and the morning of the 6th and 7th of April, that you had suggested that the bodies be removed to a place where they could be autopsied and experts could examine them. Could you explain why it was that you made the suggestion to General Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Well, quite simply, I made the suggestion because we couldn't conduct that kind of work, as I said, in the Kladovo area, and it's part of the on-site investigation that is generally done in cases of that kind. Although the order for something like that to be undertaken should be issued by the investigating judge or the prosecutor, by the organs of investigation and not the police as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: As you indicate that this kind of work is part of the on-site investigation that is generally done in cases of this sort, in your professional opinion as a senior police official, is it consistent with the criminal procedure law and with police practice to bury bodies without carrying out an autopsy?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Well, under normal conditions it is not, but in wartime conditions, there are different rules. There are always rules, but of course it depends on the prevailing situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you know whether criminal investigations, some criminal investigations, were in fact carried out during the wartime?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: You mean generally speaking?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, generally speaking.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. All this connected to crimes that were carried out. We did our job. And during the war and at that moment, that was what was done. We undertook this kind of thing to prevent profiteering and crimes during wartime too. That was the normal run of things, the proper conduct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And Mr. Golubovic, just a couple of final questions here. Have you met the accused previously? Just yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as a citizen, I did happen to meet him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And when did you first meet him? Approximately.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Well, approximately at the beginning of the 1990s when Mr. Milosevic used to undertake working visits to the copper mining and smelting plant of Bor. And in view of the post I held with regard to the security of Bor, I was in a position to see and meet him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Can you recall approximately how many times you've met the accused?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: No, I can't. I didn't count them. I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Golubovic, are you a member of a political party?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And which political party is that?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: The SPS.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Golubovic, I see that you were born in Pristina in 1937. Is this true?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is your family from Kosovo as well?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: My mother is from Kosovo, and my father is from the Timok Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When did you leave Pristina?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: We left Pristina in 1943.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So during World War II?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Why did your family leave Kosovo? In view of the years, do you remember this from the stories of your parents?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I was six or seven years old at the time. I don't have any events of my own, but I remember stories that my father was arrested then, in 1943, and that he was supposed to be transported for forced labour and that, on the way, he came out of the train and that my mother and I, at the end of 1943, also had to leave Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Regarding this event which is known as the refrigerated truck event, I see that you gave two statements, one to the working group of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Serbia on the 12th of May, 2001, and the second to the investigators of the opposite side on the 7th and 14th of August, 2002. Are these dates correct?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me whether, before you gave your statement to the members of the working group related to the incident that you are testifying about, did you have any kind of formal or informal conversation with anybody from the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So from April 1999 until --

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Except with General Djordjevic once or twice immediately after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This is what you were talking about a little while ago?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And in the meantime, you didn't have any conversations. Could you please respond precisely to this question: In this time interval from April 1999 when this affair ended in the way you described - so in the interval from April 1999 to October 2000 - did anybody from the Ministry of Internal Affairs or the previous earlier authorities forbid you from talking about it?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, which are the MUP workers from the working group who talked to you about this event? Because in this note here that I have, it just says "working group." The Official Note compiled by the working group, but it's not signed. Who talked to you?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: The working group numbered three people, and I only know Karleusa. I don't know the other two members. Perhaps they introduced themselves, but I didn't remember the names. But I know Karleusa because he was in that working group.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. What was Karleusa's post at the time that he talked to you?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I think that he was the deputy of the chief of the department, of the administration department.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Which department?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: It was the department for organised crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what his qualifications are?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: According to what I know, I think he has university degree. I'm not sure, but I think that's what he has.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And he's captain by rank.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Now he's a captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, we could establish that from the testimony here. And as far as I can see, you worked for many years in the police and you have the rank of colonel. Do you consider him to be qualified enough to conduct the investigation about this matter?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Viewing it from your point of view, according to what you said, he probably wasn't qualified enough. However, I was told that they had been entrusted by the minister to come and see me. So this is why I had this conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tasked by Minister Mihajlovic.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me whether you gave them your written statement or was this note by the working group compiled based on their interpretation of what you said?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I did not give any written statement, so it was done on the basis of our conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So can I conclude on the basis of that that the note by the working group is an interpretation of the conversation that you had with the working group?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Most probably that's how it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Since you are a police officer with a lot of experience, is it usual that when somebody's requested to provide a statement, for that person to give a written statement which is then attached to the note of the working group that is investigating something, or is this not usual?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: A written statement is customary, along with an Official Note.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you have any explanation why they did not follow the usual procedures but made an Official Note in this way, I would say in an improvised way, which is not signed and which has a sort of collective signature, "The Working Group"?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I do not. I do not have an explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And I'm interested, relating to what I have been asking you about, to what extent is this an interpretation of the working group of what you said? Can you explain to me some differences? In the statement written by the working group, they say that you allegedly contacted General Djordjevic, asked him about publishing the specific event in the "Timok Crime Review," to which he responded that that was not good. But in the statement to The Hague investigators, you say something else. Unofficially, whether you said that or not. And now you stated that you talked to Djordjevic. It doesn't matter whether it was at your own or at his initiative that this conversation was conducted, that both his or your reaction was that it was not good for this to be discussed in the press, and that this was in the jurisdiction of the bodies.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So this interpretation of theirs is quite free. And since we're dealing with this question, did I understand you correctly, since you mentioned several times the circumstances during the war, I assume that you had a lot of obligations, a lot of duties and that General Djordjevic even had more duties, was even busier because the whole country was being bombarded. At that time, did he have more important things to do and more important duties than this matter regarding the refrigerator truck?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: I assume that he did. I also had other duties. I personally didn't deal so much with that case, in view of the overall circumstances, and I assume that this applies to General Djordjevic as well. But since he's my superior, I was obliged to report to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But from conversations between you and him, the interpretation of which, even though it's paraphrased, we heard a little while ago, it comes out that both you and he were informed that representatives of responsible judiciary organs were present on the location and that it was part of their duties. So concerning the police, the police informed the judiciary organs and those organs came out to the location, and then after that you didn't really follow what they did and the things that were in their jurisdiction, but both he and you knew that the investigative organs were informed about that.

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that when the police informed the investigative organs about that, then they are authorised to order the investigative judge or public prosecutor what further actions they are to undertake relating to that matter?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that you did not consider yourself at that point to be responsible, you or Djordjevic, to carry out any further investigation regarding this matter but this was in the jurisdiction of these investigative organs who were undoubtedly informed about that? Is this so or isn't this so?

utterances.speaker: CASLAV GOLUBOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is how it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Since there was a kind of mystification here, let me just make a digression about that, how employees were paid, whether that was done in cash or in some other way. These were labourers from the local area; is that true?
